"Which is better? Alien or Aliens?" - it's like an entirely loaded question because both movies are excellent for entirely different reasons. Alien was amazing because at the time it came out it was a masterpiece of practical effects that is so good it holds up even today. It had many unknown actors that turned out to be top shelf and captured each character perfectly. It was so very easy to suspend your disbelief in that show because the atmosphere and mounting terror was so well done. The movie was a sci-fi survival horror with a strong air of suspense and quite unlike anything the world had ever seen at the time. Alien tried for a degree of realism with the characters that would never really be recaptured in any of the sequels. I'm not sure any movie has done survival horror quite as well as Alien did. Alien was proof that a horror movie could not only be amazing, but it could be elevated to an art form.

Aliens on the other hand relied more on dialogue and action than suspense and succeeded in both areas. It was a a sci-fi action movie entirely different in both tone and attitude from the first. Instead of trying to build a real atmosphere of terror, it goes for jump scares and over-the-top action sequences. The atmosphere building was rushed to make room for more action. This doesn't make it a bad movie, but it does make it a very different movie. It's less an examination of the human condition (Scott's movies are always asking a question about the human condition, Cameron's movies are action extravaganzas) and more like a battle royale that culminates in a spectacular showdown between badasses.

Both movies win for different reasons, and trying to say one is better than the other is like saying apples are better than oranges. They're both good unless you happen to hate a certain kind of fruit for some reason.

Ya know, I think you've pretty much summed it up the best. I guess my palette is more for action and explosions, that being said I did have a difficult time coming to the conclusion I liked Aliens better because Alien is one helluva movie.

In terms of raw achievement in what the movies set out to do it's very hard to rate one ahead of the other because they both nailed it, but I don't think anyone has anything to apologise for if they happen to prefer one over the other.

The movies complement each other - Aliens probably wouldn't have had nearly as much impact without the first movie setting it up. Aliens was just the next logical step for the franchise. If they had tried to recreate Alien again in the sequel it would have diminished both films.
